A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SocioSeg and SocioReasoner. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SocioSeg benchmark results, out-of-domain evaluations, ablations, inference timings and qualitative experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds multiclass segmentation results for UNet and SegFormer in Table 10.

M1.justification: The two-stage localization/refinement procedure, rendered feedback, shared VLM, frozen SAM and GRPO rewards remain unchanged. Larger VLMs and specialized multi-instance rewards are proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: v2 adds a multiclass segmentation scenario for UNet and SegFormer on the existing Socio-class and Socio-function data, extending their binary foreground-prediction evaluation. The datasets, geographic coverage and two out-of-domain scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the corresponding benchmark, generalization and reference-model comparisons is unchanged. New Table 10 evaluates the existing UNet and SegFormer baselines without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 and Table 10 add a multiclass evaluation setting for standard segmentation models alongside the retained binary setting. The existing split, metrics, model backbones, training budgets and out-of-domain procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 expands the qualitative reasoning-trace examples in Figure 13 and reports an additional error observation: models tend to segment one dominant instance. The stage, point-count and RL ablations, out-of-domain tests and five illustrated failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The three-annotator agreement study on 500 samples, its kappa of 0.854 and the training-curve reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their values. New Table 10 reports multiclass gIoU of 0.1/0.4 for UNet and 9.5/4.2 for SegFormer on Socio-class/Socio-function; these are additional settings, not same-setting score revisions. v2 also reports an instance ratio of 0.89:0.11 and 1.17 instances per image, while removing the comprehensive Socio-class performance breakdown beyond the retained top 20.

T1.justification: The method equations, GRPO objective, reward definitions and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: the SocioSeg benchmark, two-stage reinforcement-learned SocioReasoner, superior benchmark performance and zero-shot generalization. The abstract's licensing addition concerns access rather than a changed scientific claim.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.9 discusses single-instance bias and possible remedies; A.7 expands explanations involving dense map labels and ambiguous boundaries. A.8 develops application implications. Conversely, the explicit discussion of weak Training Institution and Badminton Court performance is removed; the existing error-propagation explanation moves into Section 5.2.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit Amap authorization and Apache License 2.0 statements for the dataset and code. New Figure 7 documents AOI sampling, inclusion of neighboring AOIs and verification steps. These are additional disclosures; the repository address, training settings, hardware and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Huang et al. (2018) on location-based services and expands downstream application positioning in Appendix A.8. The related-work sections and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments and application/limitations subsections, rewrites the ethics statement, relocates part of the per-category discussion and updates cross-references and publication headers. The main narrative and method exposition are largely retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 replaces line plots with two radar charts combining the existing top-20 Socio-class and Socio-function results. v2 removes the comprehensive Socio-class plot, adds construction Figure 7 and Table 10, and expands the inference-example montage from two to eight examples. Other figures and tables mainly move or receive new numbers.

improvement.justification: The multiclass check, explicit multi-instance limitation and licensing disclosures improve transparency. However, removing v1 Figure 13 and its discussion of weaker Socio-classes reduces the evidence available to assess category-level performance. With the principal results unchanged, these substantive gains and losses do not establish a reliable net improvement.
